songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: Pigpen‑driven blues set with fiery slide work and soaring Lovelight
ai_show_review.blurb: The show builds from a tentative start into a Pigpen‑heavy second half featuring a rousing Turn On Your Lovelight and intense Morning Dew. Garcia’s daring slide on Hard To Handle and Doin’ That Rag adds extra edge, while Tom Constanten’s keyboards add texture. The clear soundboard mix captures the full set without dropouts.
ai_show_review.review: On April 25, 1969 at Chicago’s Electric Theater the Dead delivered a raw, blues‑laden hour that pivots from an uncertain opening into a Pigpen‑dominated second half. Ron “Pigpen” McKernan commands the stage with a powerhouse Turn On Your Lovelight and a soulful Good Morning Little Schoolgirl, while Jerry Garcia throws caution to the wind with slide‑filled renditions of Hard To Handle and Doin’ That Rag that split opinion but kept the energy high. Phil Lesh’s bass is described as “at their very best,” anchoring the jams, and Tom Constanten adds his signature psychedelic keys (“that’s TC on keys”). The set closes on an emotionally charged Morning Dew before a brief instrumental turn‑around with Sitting On Top Of The World. Both available soundboard recordings are clear, but the Miller transfer shines with crystal‑clear balance; however, it omits a promised second set, making the full‑set capture of the first recording the recommended listen.

best_recording.reason: Clear, aggressive soundboard mix that captures the entire set without dropouts and balances Pigpen’s vocals with Garcia’s slide work.

key_highlights: Pigpen’s powerhouse Turn On Your Lovelight and Good Morning Little Schoolgirl.
Jerry Garcia’s daring slide guitar on Hard To Handle and Doin’ That Rag adds extra edge.
Intense, emotive rendition of Morning Dew that builds to a climactic finish.
Tom Constanten’s tasteful keyboard textures (‘that’s TC on keys’) enhance the psychedelic feel.
